newsitem.title: USA: Alexion says compound effective in primates.
newsitem.headline: Alexion says compound effective in primates.

text.p: Alexion Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday in a four-month primate study, treatment with its proprietary Apogen compound, MP4, reduced the severity of multiple sclerosis-like disease symptoms and prolonged the time to onset of lesions detected by magnetic resonance imaging.
Alexion also said it observed no apparent toxicity associated with the treatments.
The study was performed in common marmosets, an outbred primate species with well characterized susceptibility to autoimmune demyclinating disease, Alexion said.

"These preliminary findings represent an important extension of our ongoing studies demonstrating that parenteral (non-oral) antigen therapy can suppress manifestations of severe autoimmune disease," said Louis Matis, Vice President of Research, Immunobiology at Alexion. "We are aware of no other treatment, at this point, that has proven both safe and effective in a primate model of MS."
Alexion said it plans to file an application this year to begin clinical trials with MP4 in MS patients.
